title: Post-failover tenant undercount reconciliation and proof-of-fix
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Several customers reported missing usage for a three-hour window after a region failover. Initial traces show partial shard leader elections and interrupted KV-cache prefetch/ replay resulting in requests routed to fallback replicas that did not emit usage events to the central metering pipeline. This ticket covers full reconciliation of undercounted tokens, a long-term fix to ensure metering resiliency across failovers, and a proof-of-fix demonstrating end-to-end token emission from all replica code paths in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: Automated reconciliation script produces per-tenant corrections with signed audit log and admin preview before applying
New runtime path emits metering events from fallback replica code path for both streaming and non-streaming requests
End-to-end integration test simulates leader election + shard replay and asserts zero token loss in metering pipeline
Customer communication drafted and approved with per-tenant impact and remediation ETA
reproducible_steps: 1) Deploy runtime build with feature flag 'replica-metering-emit' disabled
2) Simulate primary shard termination to trigger leader election across 3 replicas
3) Replay in-flight streaming requests while fallback replica serves prefix without writing metering events
4) Observe missing events in kafka topic 'metering-events' and downstream aggregation delta for tenant X
investigation_notes: 2026-02-18: Pagerduty triggered by customer support; initial triage by on-call SRE (Diego Ramirez)

2026-02-19: Correlated missing 'metering-events' offsets with node failover timeline; identified that fallback replica uses fast-path that bypasses TokenAccountingEmitter under specific cache-warm states
2026-02-20: Reproducer built in staging; confirmed undercount only when KV cache prefetch is in-progress and request is re-routed mid-prefix

2026-02-22: Root cause hypothesized: optimization in runtime that skips TokenAccountingEmitter for cached-prefix fast-path to reduce latency inadvertently gated on a non-threadsafe boolean that can be false on follower replicas after failover
2026-02-24: Cross-team sync with Runtime, Metering, and Console teams; agreed on short-term reconciliation + medium-term runtime fix + long-term observability changes
proposed_fix: Short-term: run reconciliation to compute token deltas per-tenant from request logs and emit corrective metering events (admin-approve before apply)
Medium-term: modify runtime fast-path to always invoke TokenAccountingEmitter before responding, with micro-optimizations to minimize latency impact
Long-term: add invariant checks and a nightly end-to-end metering smoke test that simulates failovers and validates offsets in the metering topic
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy patched runtime with feature flag 'replica-metering-emit' enabled on staging clusters and run synthetic failover tests
Phase 2 (canary): deploy to 10% of Dedicated nodes in non-critical regions, monitor token emission and latency metrics for 48 hours
Phase 3 (gradual): roll forward to remaining Dedicated and Private customers with 1-hour blast radius and rollback playbook
Phase 4 (post-reconciliation): after runtime is stable, run reconciliation job for affected tenants and issue customer credits or corrected invoices as needed

resolution_summary: Temporary reconciliation approach implemented and dry-run validated for a pilot set of customers. Runtime patch merged to ensure TokenAccountingEmitter is invoked on fallback replica fast-paths. Canary deployment started and early metrics show corrected emission with <1% latency regression. Next steps: finish canary rollout, run full reconciliation for impacted tenants, and add nightly failover metering smoke test to CI.
